Definition: Abel hash-Shittim, a place in Palestine
BiblicalUsage: Abel-shittim — the meadow of the acacias — is named once, in Numbers 33:49, as the last camp of Israel before the Jordan: 'they pitched by Jordan, from Beth-jesimoth even unto Abel-shittim in the plains of Moab.' It is the camp where the sin of Peor happens and where Moses speaks his farewell.
TheologicalSignificance: The last camp before the crossing holds both sin and promise: Peor's shame and the plains of Moab where Moses preaches Deuteronomy. I believe that is honest about the Christian life — the ground before the Jordan is where we fail and where we hear God's word most clearly, side by side.
